summary: Both reviews require another architecture repair. The coordinate key uses an undefined/unrecomputed parent identity digest, so same physical parent/leaf can receive multiple claims. The pre-V durable claim lacks a deterministic terminal/recovery protocol, and policy issuance/execution receipt writer roles are ambiguous. The adversarial review additionally found that policy/profile/P/A/V do not bind the exact same M6 evidence set, M6.5 PASS receipt, producer/ACL/slot and P template/allow-list, enabling normal configuration cross-splice. The stricter findings control routing.

limitations: Reviews were read-only and made no product, test, contract, gate, ledger, or historical-evidence changes.
No empirical training, M6 replay, PIT certification, budget consumption, or final-OOS access occurred.

blockers: Derive the coordinate key directly from canonical DirectoryIdentity v2 and reject an unbound digest; define deterministic R→V pretransition recovery/terminal handling.
Bind policy/profile/P/A/V role-by-role to one exact M6 evidence set and immutable M6.5 PASS receipt, with one policy issuer identity and a policy-owned P template/allow-list.
Define all receipt writers explicitly, then obtain fresh independent design PASS before test design, implementation, code review, replay, M7, CCC/Gate or final OOS.
